From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Next steps: Clarify support access & break-glass for ClarityHealth

Hi Emily / Carlos —

Thanks again for a great call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed to validate so we can scope a Dedicated/Private proposal: 

1) Data residency and PII scope
- You confirmed production model inputs and outputs are US-only. Please confirm: any EU/UK customers that would change residency requirements?
- PII elements to consider: full name, DOB, SSN/Tax ID, and payment tokens. If there are other categories, list them and an example.

2) Support access model (RBAC)
- ClarityHealth prefers: "read-only access for support + ephemeral elevated access for on-call ops (break-glass)". We proposed roles in the attached access matrix draft. Please review and flag anything missing.
- Break-glass constraints: approval flow (pager/personal approval?), time limit (e.g., 30 mins), and required justification fields.

3) Logging & retention
- You asked that all break-glass events and support sessions be logged and retained for >= 2 years for audit. Confirmed? Also confirm whether log export to your SIEM is required (S3 push, syslog, or Splunk/Datadog webhook).

4) Evidence / compliance artifacts
- You requested SOC2 summary and support access evidence. We will provide a SOC2 summary and sample audit extract; please confirm the recipients (security@clarityhealth.com is fine?)

Next steps I propose:
- Emily/Carlos: review the attached access matrix and add any missing roles or scenarios (deadline: Wed Jul 28).
- Laura: we'll need a suggested RBAC mapping and a short note on how break-glass is audited.
- Vivek: technical confirmation on residency enforcement (time to replication, geo-blocking).
- Schedule a 30-min tech follow-up during the week of Aug 2 to align on logging/retention export, and run through a mock break-glass sequence.

Attachments: clarity_access_matrix_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — I’ll assemble the inputs into the mutual action plan once we have your feedback.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0136

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: for now production is US-only; we have a small pilot in Canada but that's not in scope for this procurement. Confirmed US-only for documents and logs.
- PII: add "medical record number (MRN)" to the list. Payment tokens are handled by our payment processor and should be treated as out-of-scope (we will redact).
- Support access: we want on-call engineers to have ephemeral elevated access only via a formal break-glass flow that requires two-factor approval (pager + security approval) and an automated email to security@clarityhealth.com. Time limit: 30 minutes default, with refreshable request if needed.
- Logging: yes, we need break-glass logs retained for 2 years and exported to our Splunk instance (we can accept S3 batch delivery if you support agreed encryption and key rotation).

Attached: ClarityHealth_SOC2_summary.pdf (SOC2 type II summary) — this is what our security team expects as a starting point.

We can meet on Tue Aug 3 at 10:00am PT for the tech follow-up (if that works on your side).

Emily

Emily / Marissa —

Thanks — noted and aligns with what we can support. A few concrete items from the platform side so you have a clear proposal to review: 

RBAC mapping (summary):
- Support-ReadOnly: view logs, request traces, no access to PII fields; assigned to on-call support group.
- Support-Elevated: granted for break-glass only; scoped to a single customer namespace; session provisioned with temporary tokens and full session recording.
- Security-Audit: read access to all audit trails and break-glass attestations; can request export.

Break-glass flow (proposed):
- Initiator requests break-glass via Console or API -> request goes to PagerDuty escalation to the customer security point (pager code) -> customer security must explicitly approve within the portal or via a signed webhook (2FA) -> Redwood issues ephemeral creds (30 min TTL) and starts session recording/logging.
- All actions during the elevated session are recorded and hashed; hashes and transcripts are stored encrypted.
- A signed, tamper-evident audit bundle (metadata, transcript, and session artifact references) is generated and pushed to a customer S3 bucket (or Splunk via HTTP event collector) within 15 minutes of session end.

Retention & exports:
- Default retention for break-glass artifacts: 2 years (meets your ask). We can support export to Splunk via HEC or S3 push. Encryption: server-side with customer-managed KMS (if you provide key ARN).

Pending items from you:
- Confirm the Security contact(s) who will receive pager approvals (we have security@clarityhealth.com but can add direct contacts).
- Confirm whether "Support-Elevated" sessions require video or just transcript + command history.

If useful, Vivek and I can run a short demo of the break-glass flow and show the generated audit bundle during the Aug 3 call.

Laura Bennett
Product, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
